title: Essential Bengali Nouns
summary: Common nouns for people, places, objects, and everyday life.

phrases.en: School starts at eight in the morning.
The food is on the table.
I do not have time now.
This road goes to the station.
Light is coming through the window.
The key is on the table.
My phone is in the bag.
The table is beside the window.
The chair is in front of the table.
It is ten o'clock on the clock.
Put the paper on the table.
The teacher is teaching in class.
The student is reading a book.
The doctor is at the hospital.
The shop opens at nine in the morning.
The hospital is near the city.
The bus is standing at the station.
The train comes in the morning.
The car is in front of the house.
The cat is under the chair.
The dog is playing in the garden.
There is a bird in the tree.
There is a big tree in the garden.
The sun can be seen in the sky today.
The moon is very bright at night.

phrases.bn: এই বইটা অনেক দিন পর দেখলাম।
phrases.pronunciation: Ei boi ta onek din por dekhlam.
phrases.en: I saw this book after many days.

phrases.pronunciation: Ei din ta onek bhalo gelo.

phrases.en: Today there is very little time.
There is a book on the table.
This day is full of love.
My mother is a very good person.

phrases.pronunciation: Ei kaj ta khub taratari koro.
Amader bari te pakhir basa ache.
phrases.en: There is a bird's nest in our house.

phrases.pronunciation: Ei chhele ta bhalo kaj kore.

phrases.en: Apple is very good for health.
This book is a written story.
Under the chair there is a bag.
Papaya is very good for health.
There’s a lot of work today.

phrases.bn: এই বৃষ্টিটা অনেক দিন পরে হলো।
phrases.pronunciation: Ei brishti ta onek din pore holo.

phrases.en: Protik is a very good boy.
The tree's shade is very cool.
Our house is blue in color.

phrases.context: Talking about help from a friend.

notes: Bengali nouns do not have grammatical gender.
